## Dynamical Systems


a *phase space* $x \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$, $n$ the degrees of freedom
$$\frac{d x}{dt} := \dot{x} = f(x)$$


$\Phi: T \times \mathbb{R}^n \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^n$

$\Phi(t,x)$ is the trajectory 


---

### Hamiltonian systems

$x=(p,q) \in \mathbb{R}^{2d}$

$$H(x)=T(p)+U(q)=E$$ 

degrees of freedom (dof) $2d \to 2d-1$
::: {.columns}


::: {.column}

$$\dot{p}=-\frac{\partial H}{\partial q}$$

:::

::: {.column}

$$\dot{q}=\frac{\partial H}{\partial p}$$

:::

:::



---

### Hamiltonian systems {data-transition="slide"}



$x=(p,q) \in \mathbb{R}^{2d}$, and $p,q \in \mathbb{R}^d$


$$\begin{pmatrix}\dot{p}\\\dot{q}\end{pmatrix}= \begin{pmatrix}0 & -\mathbb{1} \\ \mathbb{1} & 0\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} \tfrac{\partial H(x)}{\partial p} \\ \tfrac{\partial H(x)}{\partial q}\end{pmatrix}$$

---

### Hamiltonian systems {data-transition="slide"}

$x=(p,q) \in \mathbb{R}^{2d}$

$$\dot{x}= S \frac{\partial H(x)}{\partial x}$$



- $S= \begin{pmatrix}0 & -\mathbb{1} \\ \mathbb{1} & 0\end{pmatrix} \Rightarrow$ **symplectic geometry**: conservation of phase–space volume!

### Periodic trajectories

A trajectory is $\Phi(t,x)$ solves $\dot{x}=f(x)$: 

- periodic trajectory is if there is a period $T$, $\Phi(T,x)=x$ 

Use *surface of section* to find periodic orbits

---

### Surface of section 

$\mathcal{S}$ is a $(2d-1)$ dimensional surface, (constrained by Energy $E$)

define a $(2d-1)$-surface in phase space $\Sigma \subset \mathcal{S}$

$H(x)=E \Rightarrow p_L(E,p_R, q_L,q_R) $ 

$$\begin{align*}H(x)= T(p_L)+T(p_R) + U(q_L,q_R)&=E \\
T(p_R) + U(q_L,q_R) &\leq E \\
T(p_R) + U(\partial \mathcal{B}_{L2}, q_R) \leq E\end{align*}$$

$\Sigma = \{(p_R, q_R) | \Phi(t,x(v))=(p_L,p_R, \partial \mathcal{B}_{L2}, x_R) \}$
